samples.summary: `lensInfraReason` re-derives the reason and ignores `err.reason`, so the machine-readable `infraError` can disagree with the human summary from `lensFailureSummary`
samples.evidence: `lensFailureSummary` (line 1717) uses `err.reason || publicInfraReason({ kind, status, detail })` — preferring the string classified from the RAW upstream text, which is the only place the request id survives (redact.test.mjs:340 pins that the id reaches the PR). The newly extracted `lensInfraReason` (line 1741) unconditionally re-derives from the already-redacted `detail`: `return publicInfraReason({ kind: err.kind, status: err.status, detail: err.detail });`. For the same error the two renderers therefore emit different strings — e.g. a 529 with a request id yields `[UPSTREAM_ERROR] … (HTTP 529, req_…)` in the summary but `[UPSTREAM_ERROR] … (HTTP 529)` in `panelEntry.infraError` (the value PANEL_INFRA_ERROR pages with and eval/run.mjs stores). Worse, because it classifies a scrubbed string, a detail whose distinguishing prose was masked by the entropy rule can be re-derived into a different code than the one the producer already computed. The docblock calls it "the SECOND renderer of the same failure", which this divergence contradicts. Behaviour matches the pre-diff inline code, but the extraction was the moment to make the two consistent (`err.reason ||` would suffice).

samples.summary: `allSamplesFailedError` lets ANY never-ran sample outvote a sample where the model genuinely ran, so a real no-verdict is reclassified as infra and dropped from carry-forward — and the widened predicate makes this reachable in more cases
samples.evidence: `const infraSample = list.find((r) => sessionNeverRan(r));` marks the whole lens `infra: true` if a single sample was `api-error`/`pool-exhausted`, even when another sample carries `kind: "limit"`/`no-output` (the model ran, spent turns, produced nothing usable). The catch block then writes `{ infra: true }` (line 2839) and `prior-findings.mjs::isInfraRecord` drops the record, so the genuinely-unusable review round is not carried into the next round — precisely the #521-style false negative the new tests claim to protect against (prior-findings.test.mjs asserts the pure-`limit` case only, never the mixed one). Adding `pool-exhausted` to the predicate widens the set of siblings that can trigger this. The lens still fails closed for the round (conclusion "failure"), so impact is limited to lost carry-forward, and the first-match rule predates this diff — but the diff codifies and widens it without a mixed-sample test.
